symptomAsReported.feature: the 'One Click' parcel-identify tool in client/src/pages/DevelopmentServicesDashboard.tsx: staff click a point on the GIS map, the app queries the Bastrop-hosted Parcels_One_Click ArcGIS layer at that point, and shows the property's details.

mechanism.rootCause: BASTROP_LAYER_REGISTRY['parcels-one-click'].outFields (server/routes/esri.ts:266), a single hardcoded field list shared by BOTH the v1 session-gated /api/esri/one-click-at-point route and the v2 platformOneClickAtPoint() helper, has requested a field named 'Ordinance_Link' since 2026-03-05 (git blame e82f0c28). The City of Bastrop's own ArcGIS Online-hosted layer (services7.arcgis.com/qOeXJdBtGknaCJC4, Parcels_One_Click/FeatureServer/23) had its schema edited 2026-09-10T20:24:42Z (live editingInfo.schemaLastEditDate) and no longer has that field. ArcGIS FeatureServer queries reject the ENTIRE outFields list with HTTP 400 ('outFields parameter is invalid') when even one requested field name does not exist -- there is no partial-field degrade. Every One Click query has failed since 2026-09-10.
mechanism.whyItLookedLikeSilence: The v1 route correctly surfaces the ArcGIS error as a 502, but the client's fetchOneClickAtPoint treats any non-{found:true,data:...} response identically to 'no parcel here' -- it clears all one-click state and shows nothing, no visible error. That matches the reported symptom exactly: staff click a parcel and nothing happens.
mechanism.externalNotInternal: This is an external GIS-provider schema change, not application code drifting on its own.

secondMechanismConsideredAndRejected.hypothesis: The dispatch's own leading hypothesis: d2d3648 (#40, 'exempt /platform from the session-auth gate') broadened the global auth-gate's public-prefix match and let it bleed into unintended paths, breaking session resolution for the v1 one-click route.
secondMechanismConsideredAndRejected.whyRejected: Read the full diff. It adds exactly one literal string, '/platform', to a startsWith() allowlist. '/api/esri/one-click-at-point' and '/api/property-intelligence/summary' do not start with '/platform' or any other allowlisted prefix, so req.path.startsWith(p) cannot match them -- confirmed by reading the match logic, not by assumption. Diffed server/routes.ts across the ENTIRE seam (68fe8cc^..332a16c): this one-line prefix addition is the only non-additive change in the file. No session-gated v1 route's auth requirement changed. Separately falsified 332a16c (#52, wastewater geometry): it touches only the wastewater branch of platformQueryPropertyIntelLayer, never platformOneClickAtPoint or the parcels-one-click registry entry.
secondMechanismConsideredAndRejected.timelineAlsoFalsifiesIt: smartcity-api-00138-law (the seam's final revision) was created 2026-09-04T20:41:32Z per gcloud run revisions describe (field-read). The external ArcGIS schema changed 2026-09-10T20:24:42Z -- six days after the seam had already been serving unchanged. Bastrop reported the symptom the morning of 2026-09-14 -- four days after the external change. The operator's framing ('the v2 import broke the version one dashboard') does not fit this symptom's timeline. Reported as a correction per DEV_PROCESS 3.2, not concealed: the seam PRs did real, separate, and apparently correct work (auth exemption, GIS parity); they simply are not the cause of this particular customer report.

limitationNamedHonestly: The v1 /api/esri/one-click-at-point route itself requires a real staff OIDC session (Replit Auth) that this lane does not hold credentials for; creating or bypassing one was out of scope and not attempted. Verification instead relies on (1) direct code comparison showing the v1 route and platformOneClickAtPoint() construct the identical ArcGIS query against the identical BASTROP_LAYER_REGISTRY['parcels-one-click'] object, and (2) that shared object being verified live, both broken and fixed, through two independently-routed, live, production v2 endpoints, plus the raw ArcGIS source itself. This is reported as a proxy verification of the v1 UI, not claimed as a literal browser click-through.
falsifier: The exact ArcGIS query the app issues, run against the real Bastrop-hosted layer both with and without the dead field name, at a real coordinate, both directly and through the live deployed application before and after the traffic shift.
contradicted: The dispatch's and operator's leading hypothesis that PRs #39-52 (the smartcity-dashboards platform seam) broke v1. Neither ranked hypothesis (auth-gate exemption, wastewater geometry) touches the code path involved, and the timeline (seam finished 2026-09-04; external schema changed 2026-09-10; report came 2026-09-14) places the actual cause after the seam had already been serving unchanged for six days.
leave_behind: platformOneClickAtPoint() (v2) silently swallows an ArcGIS query error into a plain null result (`if (data.error || ...) return null`), unlike the v1 route which correctly surfaces a 502. This is a DEV_PROCESS 4.3 silent-fallback pattern -- it is what let the v2 platform route degrade invisibly for five days before Bastrop's own report surfaced the same underlying break on the v1 side. Same root cause as this incident, not a second defect from the seam; worth a small follow-up (surface the error, or at least log it) but not fixed here since it was not the reported symptom and touching more of the platform-internal error handling than the one dead field risks the dispatch's own hard constraint against breaking v2.

The three decision records the fourteen seam PRs cite but that do not exist in doc_repo (2026-09-03_smartcity_os_platform_read_authorization.md, 2026-09-03_bastrop_tx_dashboards_pack_ratified.md, and a 2026-09-04 Leaflet-island override), and that none of that work carries a plan row -- named again per the dispatch's own instruction; not this lane's to close.
G-131 (property-intel/summary's bare numeric DEFAULT_TENANT_ID literal) is unrelated to this incident and was not touched, per the dispatch's explicit demotion of 0e5c41e.

This is a live external dependency: the City of Bastrop's own GIS organization can silently rename/remove fields on layers this app depends on with no notice to this codebase, and ArcGIS's all-or-nothing outFields validation means one dropped field takes down the whole query with no partial degrade. Worth a structural fix (validate the registry's outFields against each layer's live schema on a schedule, or catch and log a specific 'field missing' signal instead of a generic 500/silent-null) -- proposed, not built, per DEV_PROCESS 5.4 (propose, do not unilaterally remediate structural changes beyond the incident).
